issues.title: Type mismatch in total_price initialization breaks Decimal arithmetic
issues.description: The total_price field is initialized with integer 0 instead of Decimal(0), creating a type inconsistency. The MessageAgentThought model defines total_price as Mapped[Decimal | None] expecting a Decimal type, and other price fields (message_unit_price, answer_unit_price, etc.) are correctly initialized with Decimal types. This inconsistency will cause type errors during price calculations when the system attempts to perform Decimal arithmetic operations (addition, multiplication) between Decimal and int types, potentially breaking billing computations or causing runtime exceptions.

issues.title: Tool responses replaced with tool inputs in agent history organization
issues.description: In the organize_agent_history method, when building ToolPromptMessage objects, the content is incorrectly populated from tool_inputs dictionary instead of tool_responses dictionary. This means the LLM will receive the tool's input parameters as if they were the tool's output/response. For example, if a tool was called with {"query": "weather in NYC"}, the agent history would show this input dict as the tool's response instead of the actual weather data. This breaks the agent's ability to learn from previous tool executions and will cause incorrect context to be passed to subsequent LLM calls.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #27749 - refactor(models): Refine MessageAgentThought SQLAlchemy typing

structured_output.summary:
The PR moves `MessageAgentThought` from `Base` to `TypeBase` (a `MappedAsDataclass`), adds explicit `Mapped[...]` annotations, and makes `id`/`created_at` init-only. It also changes `create_agent_thought` to pass `Decimal` prices and `CreatorUserRole.ACCOUNT`, makes thought accumulation None-safe, and refactors the agent-history reconstruction in `base_agent_runner.py`. The model typing work is sound, and the test edits are a necessary consequence of `init=False` on `id`.

However, the PR introduces two correctness regressions. The history reconstruction now sends tool *inputs* where tool *responses* belong, so every multi-turn agent conversation with tool calls gets wrong context fed to the LLM. The price defaults are also set asymmetrically: the answer side now gets a 0.001 unit price where it previously had 0. Neither is covered by tests, and the PR adds an unused Pydantic model with a misleading comment.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The tool-response regression changes what the LLM sees in agent history on every tool-using conversation, and the price-field asymmetry changes cost calculations. Both are silent, and no test would catch them. These need fixing before merge; the typing refactor itself is fine.

architecture.overview:
Agent runs persist each reasoning/tool step as a `MessageAgentThought` row. `BaseAgentRunner.create_agent_thought` inserts a row before the tool executes, `save_agent_thought` updates it with the thought, tool name, input and observation, and `organize_agent_history` later rebuilds prior turns as `AssistantPromptMessage` / `ToolPromptMessage` entries to replay into the next LLM call. The model lives in `api/models/model.py` and was a plain declarative `Base`, so its constructor did not validate required fields.

This PR switches the model to `TypeBase` (`MappedAsDataclass`). That makes the constructor a generated dataclass `__init__`: `id` and `created_at` drop out of it, `created_by`/`created_by_role` become required, and the price columns take `Decimal`. The runner changes follow from that: it passes enum and `Decimal` values and rebuilds history with a None-safe parser. The history parser is where the regression sits.
steps: Entry point: `BaseAgentRunner.create_agent_thought` (base_agent_runner.py ~302-342) constructs a `MessageAgentThought` with explicit prices, role and ids, then commits it and returns the generated id.
Accumulation: `save_agent_thought` (~344-370) appends streamed thought text. The PR makes this None-safe, so a row created with `thought=None` no longer raises on `+=`.

Model: `MessageAgentThought` (model.py ~1838-1880) is now a `TypeBase` with `Mapped[...]` columns. `id` uses `default_factory` and `init=False`, and `created_at` is `init=False` with a server default. Only the test file's `id=` kwargs needed to be removed, since nothing else constructs this model.

History replay: `organize_agent_history` (~455-520) rebuilds tool calls from `tool_input` (arguments) and `observation` (responses). The PR changes the `ToolPromptMessage` content from `tool_responses.get(...)` to `tool_inputs.get(...)`, so `tool_responses` is parsed and then never read.

Net effect: the typing and constructor changes are consistent with each other, but the price defaults and the history content lookup need correction before the data reaching the LLM and the cost columns can be trusted.

findings.title: Tool response content is built from tool inputs
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py`, inside `organize_agent_history` (around lines 500-504), the `ToolPromptMessage` content was changed from `tool_responses.get(tool, agent_thought.observation)` to `str(tool_inputs.get(tool, agent_thought.observation))`. Restore it to read from `tool_responses`, so the replayed tool message contains the observation rather than the arguments. Keep the `str(...)` wrapper only if the observation can be non-string. Then confirm `tool_responses` is read, and add a unit test that builds history from a thought with a known `tool_input` and `observation` and asserts the ToolPromptMessage content equals the observation.

findings.title: Price defaults are asymmetric between message and answer sides
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py`, `create_agent_thought` (around lines 319-326) sets `message_unit_price=Decimal(0)` and `message_price_unit=Decimal("0.001")` but `answer_unit_price=Decimal("0.001")` and `answer_price_unit=Decimal(0)`. The original code set all four to 0. Make the message and answer sides consistent: decide the intended unit price and price-unit values, and apply the same pattern to both sides. Check how `api/core/tools/utils/model_invocation_utils.py` (around lines 120-165) fills these fields later so the defaults match what usage recording expects. Also replace `total_price=0` with `Decimal(0)` to match the `Numeric` / `Decimal` typing this PR is introducing.

findings.title: Unused AgentThoughtValidation model with a misleading comment
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py`, remove the unused `AgentThoughtValidation` class (around lines 52-65) and the `from pydantic import BaseModel` import it depends on, unless it is actually intended to validate data in `create_agent_thought` or `save_agent_thought`. If it is kept, use `model_config = ConfigDict(extra=...)` rather than the Pydantic v1 `class Config`, and make the comment match the chosen behavior.

findings.title: No test covers the changed history-replay or thought-creation logic
findings.fixPrompt: Add tests for `BaseAgentRunner` in `api/tests` (near the existing agent tests). Cover: (1) `organize_agent_history` produces a `ToolPromptMessage` whose content equals the stored observation for each tool, and an `AssistantPromptMessage` with the thought when there are no tools; (2) `create_agent_thought` persists `CreatorUserRole.ACCOUNT` and the expected price values; (3) `save_agent_thought` appends to a `None` thought without raising. Assert on observable values, not mock call counts.

findings.title: Thought accumulation is now None-safe
findings.body:
`save_agent_thought` used to do `agent_thought.thought += thought`, which raises `TypeError` when the column is `None`. It now treats a missing value as an empty string before appending, which matches the new `Mapped[str | None]` typing. This is a small but real fix.

::diff{file="api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py" lines="364-367"}

findings.title: Model typing and constructor changes are consistent
findings.body:
Moving `MessageAgentThought` to `TypeBase` and annotating every column with `Mapped[...]` is consistent with the other migrated models in `model.py`, which already use `TypeBase`. Making `id` and `created_at` `init=False` stops callers from setting them, and the only constructor call site outside tests is `create_agent_thought`. `created_by_role=CreatorUserRole.ACCOUNT` is a `StrEnum`, so it stores the same string `"account"` the old code wrote. Keeping `server_default` on the `price_unit` columns while also giving them a Python default is a sensible belt-and-braces setup.

::diff{file="api/models/model.py" lines="1838-1848"}
